design_rationale:
[0. Step 0 draw and scope snapshot] scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]}. Tree: root listing_ext_pricing_assist_rate (6 factors) with prerequisite problems listing_ext_minimum_stay_floor (4) and listing_ext_extra_guest_fee_ceiling (4). Task 0 occupies the three per-stay fee policies of a Denver suite. This task claims the per-night pricing of a Nashville house with tools raise_minimum_stay_1aeaa300 (agent), reset_extra_guest_fee_9609655d (agent) and save_nightly_rate_d0fc8a90 (user). It reads the cleaning fee but never writes it. All six extended policies are claimed, each by one task.

[R2. Revision record, audit round 1 -> round 2]
 - G-1 / T1-1 (method factors that were multipliers): the extra-guest "plan phase-in" share (0.5 / 0.75 / 1) and the Pricing Assist "assessment confidence" share (0.5 / 0.75 / 1) were replaced.
   - Extra-guest: a damage look-back by party record. A party_violation strike within twelve months lengthens the property-damage window to 36 months, one 12-24 months back to 24 months, otherwise the standard 12. Large extra-guest parties are where party damage arises, and the party ban applies to every space type.
   - Pricing Assist: an expected stay length. With 10+ stays on the latest Superhost assessment, the cleaning fee is spread over the mean of the minimum stay and the account's average stay; with 1-9 stays, over the mean of the minimum stay and weekly_discount_min_nights; otherwise over the minimum stay alone. Pricing engines amortise the cleaning fee over the stay they expect.
   - Both change which records or which divisor are used, not a multiplier. The rating adjustment now reads the assessment of the last three months, so the listing history stays load-bearing. The adjustment values were rescaled (rating 0.04/0.02, demand 0.04/0.02, Superhost 0.02, responsiveness 0.01/-0.02, age -0.03/-0.02) and the standard extra-guest share is 0.70.
 - G-8 (plan phase-in weakly motivated): removed (see above).
 - T1-2 (strike without a suspension on record): the 2026-07-05 strike concerned the loft. Its safety suspension is now on record through the approved reinstatement request decided 2026-07-30, and the reinstatement read is by host (customer_id), so the agent sees both requests. The loft's minimum stay is 4, equal to its own floor, so nothing is owed there. The house's floor still reads only the house's own reinstatement (scoped by listing).
 - T1-3 (the extra-guest reset uses the post-cut rate while the host then raises the rate): left as is. Both prerequisite sentences fix the order, so there is no second reading. After the host saves 446.11 the extra-guest ceiling would be RND(446.11 / 6 x 0.96, 2) = 71.38, above the reset fee of 63.20, and the host may raise his own fee later; a support reset never raises a fee on its own.
 - Every downstream asset was updated in the same pass: initial_state, evaluation_criteria (63.20 / 446.11, reinstatement read by customer, necessities), computations, prerequisite_closure, solvability_contract and this dossier.

[1. Why this is a good test] Jalen asks for one thing: set his house to the nightly price Roamhaven suggests, which he saves himself. Pricing Assist prices the all-in night of a full party (rate + cleaning fee spread over the expected stay + extra-guest charges beyond the threshold) and moves it by five record-based adjustments. The rule works the suggestion out only after the minimum stay stands at or above its floor, and fixes it only after the extra-guest fee stands at or below its ceiling; neither holds today.
 - A party strike (2026-07-05) and an approved property-damage claim (approved 2026-06-24) raised the floor to 3 nights while the minimum stay is 2.
 - The host's rate cut on 2026-09-08 pulled the per-guest ceiling to 63.20, below the 70.00 fee.
 The agent must find both owed corrections and compute them from host strikes, HostCover claims and plan level, the house's own reinstatement record and its quality history. It books them and then computes the root on the corrected world: 446.11 (449.10 on the opening world).

[2. Policies, lineage, triggers] Subjects [listing_pricing_updated, listing_fee_change_logged]. base_policy_refs include listing_evt_fee_settings and listing_evt_discounts (eligibility []) plus input lineage: the floor adds safety_standards, reinstatement and quality_assessment; the extra-guest ceiling adds safety_standards; Pricing Assist adds quality_assessment. Overwrites: the floor supersedes 'Minimum stay settings must lie between minimum_nights_floor and minimum_nights_ceiling'; the extra-guest ceiling supersedes 'extra_guest_fee no higher than extra_guest_fee_max_usd' (the space-type maximum still caps it); Pricing Assist overwrites nothing. The floor raise and the extra-guest reset are state_due; Pricing Assist is on_request.

[3. Factor card] (frozen_time 2026-09-29)
Minimum-stay floor (baseline 1; gold 3):
 - party_strike_nights [parameter, cross host]: c669bce6-2c8d-4fb9-93b8-f420974ef8b6 (2026-07-05) is in 12 months -> 1; near-miss 86356bbe-9000-4c3a-b72f-264f5d333190 (15 months). Baseline -> 2.
 - property_damage_nights [parameter, cross protect]: b78ceacc-f5b6-4cca-8cb3-c0b64f17ead8 -> 1; near-misses 25ad0f29-d24c-4cd1-ba1e-3ec58153bb78 (15 months) and dab5ed95-fe4a-414b-8c91-1431dd53da12 (denied). Baseline -> 2.
 - safety_reinstatement_nights [parameter, history+date]: the house's 1e9b0778-c59d-47c3-a288-714a20bd2121 was decided 2025-07-18 (14 months) -> 1; the loft's 41cb8f75-0087-4559-8599-bd20750e6579 (2026-07-30) is another listing's request and is excluded by listing. Baseline -> 2.
 - party_nights_assessment_record [method]: four passes in 12 months -> 3 nights halved, half night up -> 2; baseline (as is) -> 4.
Extra-guest ceiling (baseline 395/6 x 0.70 = 46.08; gold 63.20):
 - damage_lookback_by_party_record [method: window convention, cross host]: strike within 12 months -> 36 months; baseline 12 months -> 58.59.
 - damage_loss_addition [parameter, cross protect]: losses in 36 months 3550.00 -> 0.15; baseline -> 53.33.
 - per_claim_limit_addition [parameter]: Standard 25000.00 -> 0.05; baseline -> 59.91.
 - income_loss_addition [parameter]: Standard pays 0 nights -> 0.06; baseline -> 59.25.
Pricing Assist (baseline = current rate 395.00; gold 446.11):
 - expected_stay_length [method, cross host]: latest Superhost assessment 75a166b3-a782-4397-b5de-e3f44c1d9b2d 64 stays / 212 nights -> (3 + 3.3125) / 2 = 3.15625; baseline (minimum stay 3) -> 446.41.
 - rating_adjustment [parameter, multi-source]: 8971dd34-3fed-491e-86de-c27f6498200a 4.86 with 14 reviews -> 0.04; baseline -> 416.91.
 - demand_adjustment [parameter, cross host]: 212 nights -> 0.02; near-miss a8784886-598a-4194-a06e-1933bb0bab8c (older, 205). Baseline -> 431.51.
 - superhost_adjustment [parameter, cross host]: Superhost -> 0.02; baseline -> 431.51.
 - responsiveness_adjustment [parameter, cross host]: 99.0 -> 0.01; baseline -> 438.81.
 - listing_age_adjustment [parameter, date]: 19 months -> -0.02; baseline -> 460.72.
Each computation has >= 2 parameter factors and >= 1 honest method factor. The halving rule rounds up; the window and stay-length conventions change which records or which divisor are used. Every factor moves its result.

[4. Base-invariant card] Only policy_scope entries (listing_evt_fee_settings and listing_evt_discounts carry no eligibility); no time gate. Inherited clauses hold: no stay exists that a change could alter; one record per changed value; threshold, discounts and cleaning fee untouched; the suggestion lies within 10.00-25000.00; listing listed, account active.

[5. Business-object card] Target listing dbae6bad-7183-4ada-bd98-65d7ab113c1a (Entire Home, "East Nashville 4BR, Hot Tub & Big Porch"); plan 9744e045-c95f-4c1e-8c22-0758d80704be. Excluded by visible keys: the loft 6acdf2b3-393f-4ebc-8ca5-b7ef8fc1c8c3, its plan 854667ef-7805-40b1-bbb4-a1984f069f5e and its reinstatement request; the denied claim; strikes and claims outside each window. Account-level rows (strikes, Superhost assessments, travel credit) are keyed by host_account_id. Every claim is settled: Standard reimbursements 2100 x 0.8 - 250 = 1430.00 and 1450 - 250 = 1200.00, plus one denial. No restriction from strikes: they are 386 days apart.

[6. Seed rows] Identity; the Superhost account (since 2025-10-01) with 2 strikes, 2 Superhost assessments and the 2026-Q2 travel credit; the house (minimum stay 2, extra-guest fee 70.00 on the wrong side of today's floor and ceiling) and the loft (minimum stay 4 = its floor). Six change records, each valid on its day: extra-guest 55.00 on 2025-03-01 (ceiling 60.75) and 70.00 on 2026-06-25 (76.80); minimum stay 5 on 2025-07-20 (floor 5) and 2 on 2026-06-16 (floor 2). Six quarterly assessments since the house was first listed (2025-Q1 not_assessed). Two reinstatement requests (house 2025, loft 2026). The Standard plan with 3 property-damage claims and their records. Removing b78ceacc-f5b6-4cca-8cb3-c0b64f17ead8 lowers the floor to 2 and the extra-guest ceiling to 58.59 (one claim, 2100.00 -> 0.08). Removing the 2026-09-08 cut puts the ceiling at 76.80, so no reset would be owed.

[7. Problem-tree card] Root listing_ext_pricing_assist_rate (on_request, owner user).
 - -> listing_ext_minimum_stay_floor, value_input (gate cleaning_per_night), form state, negated: "A suggested nightly rate is not worked out until the minimum stay on the listing stands at or above the listing's minimum-stay floor." Only raise_minimum_stay_1aeaa300 writes the minimum stay. False at opening: 2 against 3. Deletion: 447.20.
 - -> listing_ext_extra_guest_fee_ceiling, value_input (gate all_in_night), form state, affirmative: "The suggested nightly rate is fixed only after the extra-guest fee on the listing stands at or below the listing's extra-guest ceiling." Only reset_extra_guest_fee_9609655d writes it. False at opening: 70.00 against 63.20. Deletion: 448.02.
 Both edges pass the four-point test. They commute (hash e247dad279672137... in both orders). value_input edges: 2. The customer's own write is the root save. No hint in user_scenario, and no tool validates a prerequisite.

[8. Persona] Jalen volunteers his goal and name; gives phone 6155552716 and ID 2049 when asked; agrees passively to corrections; saves exactly the figure handed over; hangs up after saving.

[9. Easy mistakes] Computing on the opening world (449.10) or after one correction (447.20 / 448.02). Taking the current rate (395.00). Counting the 2025 strike or claim in 12-month windows, the denied claim anywhere, or the loft's reinstatement for the house. Using the standard 12-month damage look-back (58.59). Spreading the cleaning fee over the minimum stay alone (446.41). Reading the loft's Essential plan. Rounding the halved nights down. Saving the rate as an agent write.

[10. Standard solution] find_customers -> verify -> find_listings -> find_listing_events(house) -> find_listing_reinstatement_requests(customer) -> find_host_accounts -> find_host_account_events -> find_protection_plans -> find_protection_claims(house) -> find_protection_events(house plan) -> raise minimum stay to 3 -> reset extra-guest fee to 63.20 -> hand over; Jalen saves 446.11.

[11. Verification] Gate sandbox, writes applied in order: floor 3, ceiling 63.20, suggestion 446.11. Factor baselines: floor 2/2/2/4 (all 1); ceiling 58.59/53.33/59.91/59.25 (all 46.08); suggestion 446.41/416.91/431.51/431.51/438.81/460.72 (all 395.00). Prerequisite sensitivity 447.20 / 448.02 / 449.10. Historical saves recomputed as of their dates with the rate of that day. Other state_due policies on 2026-09-29: house pet 310.00 vs 0.00 and cleaning 788.00 vs 260.00; loft floor 4 = 4 and extra-guest 81.27 vs 20.00 - none owed. Per-task gates (--task 1) re-run after the round-2 rework: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK; traceability deferred until the KB is rendered.

[12. Closure] floor -> raise_minimum_stay_1aeaa300 -> step 11 minimum_nights 3; extra-guest -> reset_extra_guest_fee_9609655d -> step 13 extra_guest_fee 63.2; Pricing Assist -> save_nightly_rate_d0fc8a90 -> step 15 nightly_rate 446.11; three records dated 2026-09-29. Scope and required_documents list the three policies in order.

[13. Draft from visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas, persona and finder returns the same actions, order class and values follow: the root names its two waited-on states, the floor and ceiling rules give 3 and 63.20, and the root gives 446.11 saved by the host.

[14. Manual values gates] Two hops over listing, host and protect records; an owner=user save of the host's own price; need, authorisation and write boundary explicit; facts grounded in initial_state; one frozen_time. The prerequisite sentences pass the four-point test, in both directions. compute_basis is complete in both directions. Method labels are honest, and baselines are exactly the baseline paragraphs.
user_scenario:
You are Jalen Whitmore, a music producer in Nashville who hosts two places on Roamhaven under your own host account: a four-bedroom house in East Nashville, listed as "East Nashville 4BR, Hot Tub & Big Porch", and a one-bedroom loft in Germantown. You're laid-back and talk in short bursts, calling from the studio.

Your reason for calling: summer was busy, and when things slowed down earlier this month you dropped the house's nightly price on a hunch. Now you'd rather not guess - you've heard Roamhaven can work out a suggested nightly price for a listing, and you want the East Nashville house set to exactly the nightly price Roamhaven suggests. You don't know what it will be and you won't name a number. Prices are your call, so you want the agent to tell you the figure and hand the change over so you can put it in yourself from your listing editor. This is only about the house, not the loft.

You start with your name and what you want. When the agent asks to confirm your identity, you give the mobile number on your profile, 6155552716; if they want one more detail, you give the last four characters of the ID you verified with, 2049. If they still need more, you can give your date of birth, 1988-02-17, or your email, jwhitmore.music@outlook.com. If asked which listing, you say the East Nashville house and read its title.

If the agent tells you that some other setting on the house has to be changed first, or that support is going to change one of your settings to match Roamhaven's rules, you're a bit taken aback but you say fine, if that's how it works, go ahead; you don't argue the numbers, you don't ask for an exception and you don't bring up any setting yourself. If the agent asks whether you want anything else changed, you say no, just the nightly price.

When the agent gives you the suggested nightly price and hands the change over, you save it on the house with exactly that amount and say it went through. Once it's saved, you thank them and hang up.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's Roamhaven profile from the full name and mobile number he gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the host's customer reference number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller with two stated credentials: the mobile number and the last four characters of his verified ID.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be confirmed before any listing setting is read or changed; two matching credentials are the threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host's listings and pick the East Nashville Entire Home: nightly rate, cleaning fee, minimum stay, extra-guest fee and threshold, max guests, first_listed_date; the Germantown loft is not the target.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The all-in night of Pricing Assist is built from these settings; the minimum stay is compared with its floor and the extra-guest fee with its ceiling (per-guest portion = nightly rate / threshold); first_listed_date decides the listing age adjustment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the house's change log and its quarterly quality assessments.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The assessments decide the assessment record of the party-prevention nights (all passes in twelve months) and the rating adjustment (the assessment of the last three months: average 4.86, 14 reviews); the change log shows the 2026-09-08 rate cut that left the extra-guest fee above its ceiling and the 2026-06-16 minimum-stay change.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host's reinstatement requests: the house's approved request after its 2025 safety suspension (decided 2025-07-18) and the loft's approved request after its 2026 safety suspension.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement nights of the house's minimum-stay floor read the most recent approved safety reinstatement of the house itself (14 months old); the loft's 2026 request belongs to another listing and does not count.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host account: tier Superhost, status active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The Superhost adjustment of Pricing Assist reads the tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the account ledger: the two party_violation strikes and the two most recent Superhost assessments with their nights and response rates.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Strike nights count party strikes in the last 12 months (the 2026-07-05 strike); the same strike lengthens the extra-guest damage look-back to 36 months; the expected stay length, demand and responsiveness read the most recent Superhost assessment (64 stays, 212 nights, 99.0 percent).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the HostCover plans and pick the house's active Standard plan (effective 2025-02-14).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The per-claim limit and income-loss additions of the extra-guest ceiling read the level of the house's active plan (HostCover Standard); the loft's Essential plan is not the house's.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the HostCover claims on the house: property_damage claims, their status, filing dates and verified losses.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Damage nights count approved property_damage claims in 12 months; the damage-loss addition adds up verified losses of approved property_damage claims within the 36-month look-back; the denied March 2026 claim counts in neither.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the house plan's ledger: payment requests, the two reimbursements and the denial.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms the two property_damage claims were decided and paid and the third denied, so only approved claims are counted and none is still open.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the support tool that sets a listing's minimum stay.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the minimum-stay raise; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the house's minimum stay from 2 to its minimum-stay floor of 3 nights and log the change.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: listing_ext_minimum_stay_floor: the minimum stay stands below the floor and is owed a raise; Pricing Assist is not worked out until the minimum stay stands at or above that floor, and it spreads the cleaning fee over the raised minimum stay.
